overall_structure.value: For the 15Al (Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu at.%) low-density steel after aging at 525 °C for 10 h, the microstructure is essentially a β-Mn matrix produced by the α→β-Mn transformation (the α matrix had been almost completely transformed into β-Mn within 3 h of aging at 525 °C), with fine new precipitates revealed within the β-Mn in the 10 μm SE inset. The transformation from the single-phase α (BCC) solution-treated state to the aged state produced a hardness rise from 253.4 HV to 915.7 HV.

source.reason: The 15Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 10 h is the 525 °C/10 h condition of the 15Al alloy, whose hardness (915.7 ± 9.5 HV) and SE microstructure (Fig. 7) are reported; the aged microstructure is dominated by β-Mn formed by the α→β-Mn transformation.

unmapped_findings: For the 15Al alloy the elastic modulus E = 164 GPa (measured through compressive stress-strain curves) is reported and used in the indentation fracture-toughness equation (Eq. 1); this modulus is given for the 15Al alloy generally and is not reported specifically for the 525 °C/10 h sample.

The 15Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 10 h corresponds to the 10 h endpoint of the 525 °C series in Fig. 2; the 15Al hardness contour map shows a large >900 HV field covering most aging times above ~3 h and high temperatures, consistent with the 915.7 HV measured at 525 °C/10 h.

The specific hardness of 141 HV·cm3/g and the fracture toughness of 8.6 MPa·m1/2 for the 15Al alloy refer to its peak-hardness state (965.6 HV, achieved at 600 °C for 6 h), not to the 525 °C/10 h sample.
